title: Prospective vs. Retrospective Safety Evaluation Design

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: pre-registration improves evaluation credibility by preventing post-hoc tuning. Gap: this addresses methodology norms rather than directly preventing safety failures.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training a small model from scratch and conducting prospective evaluation requires advanced ML skills well beyond a beginner CS student level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multi-phase project: pre-register, train model, evaluate, compare with post-hoc claims. Each phase has significant overhead, well beyond 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: The general problem of prospective vs retrospective evaluation is well-discussed in medical AI (only 2% of ML health studies are prospective), and the need for pre-registration in AI research is recognized. However, no published work was found that specifically designs and executes a prospective pre-registered safety evaluation of an LLM to compare against retrospective analysis. The concept is discussed as a need but not experimentally demonstrated for AI safety.
